/** * A composable feedback controller whose terms are selected with a fluent API. * *

Each call that starts on this controller creates an independent calculation. For example: * * 

{@code
 * Scalar response = controller.p().d().s().calculate(error);
 * Scalar responseWithFeedforward = controller.p().vel(velocity).accel(acceleration)
 *         .calculate(error);
 * }
* *

The terminal {@link Calculation#calculate(double)} call samples and updates the controller's * derivative state once, regardless of which terms are selected. */

files.name: PDSController
files.doc:
/** * A general purpose PD controller with static friction compensation specifically made for * controlling robot movement in a one-dimensional axis. * *
    *
  • kP - proportional gain (how aggressively the controller responds to error)
    • *
  • kD - derivative gain (how much the controller accounts for error rate of change)
    • *
  • kS - minimum power (a constant power added in the error's direction to overcome * static forces)
    • *
* *

The controller applies the full static-friction term outside a small target deadband and * removes it inside that deadband. This preserves breakaway authority without causing target * jitter. * *

Special thanks to Wolfpack Machina (18438) for inspiration for this controller * * @author Dylan B. - 18597 RoboClovers - Delta * @author DrPixelCat - 7842 alum */

files.name: AdaptiveKalmanFilter
files.doc:
/**
 * A two-state linear Kalman filter designed for robotic kinematics (e.g., tracking [Velocity, Acceleration]).
 *
 * Unlike standard Kalman filters that require static, manually tuned Q and R covariance matrices,
 * this filter uses an innovation-based adaptive estimator. It watches the statistical spread of the
 * incoming data to learn the actual sensor noise (R) and monitors its own prediction errors (NIS)
 * to dynamically scale the process trust (Q).
 *
 * The two-state model, timing and noise adaptation wrap the shared {@link KalmanFilter} core.
 *
 * @author Joel H - 7842a
 */
